```markdown
**RE: Member appeal of adverse benefit determination — request for reconsideration**

- **Member name:** Emerson Hayes
- **Member ID:** W807153430
- **Plan:** Harvard Pilgrim Health Care (Commercial/ACA), Massachusetts
- **Reference number:** POC-9668BA39E4-60948
- **Date of denial notice:** August 4, 2026
- **Service denied:** Knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery, CPT 29881
- **Treating surgeon:** Marchetti, MD, orthopedic surgery
- **Governing policy:** Evolent Knee Arthroscopy Prior Authorization Tip Sheet (Evolent_CG-316), https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2024-02/2023%20Knee%20Arthroscopy%20Clin%20Tip%20Sheet%20Evolent%2002282024.pdf

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of my knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery (CPT 29881), which the plan denied in its notice dated August 4, 2026. The notice states that the clinical records do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision, because the records that were already submitted document both the conservative treatment the policy describes and a finding for which the policy says conservative treatment is not required.

Below I have quoted the plan's own criteria from the Evolent Knee Arthroscopy Prior Authorization Tip Sheet (Evolent_CG-316) and matched each one to what is in my medical records. My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed.

---

### 1. The policy states that conservative treatment is not required in certain situations, and my records describe one of them

The policy states:

> "Non-operative treatment for meniscal tears is not required in the following situations:"

Among the situations it then lists:

> "History of acute injury/onset of symptoms with a locked knee and/or mechanical symptoms of locking; Physical examination demonstrates ANY positive meniscal findings on examination or demonstrates evidence of a locked knee (loss of terminal extension); MRI demonstrates a bucket-handle tear of the meniscus. (Does not include an extruded meniscus or flap tears)"

My records establish these findings:

- My MRI of the knee dated May 24, 2026 shows a **displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking**.
- My examination documents **positive provocative testing on the affected side**, with range of motion limited by pain.
- My function is documented as **locking and giving way**; I cannot squat or kneel, and I am limited to level walking.

The policy itself says non-operative treatment is not required in these situations. On the plan's own terms, the reason given for the denial — an inadequate trial of conservative treatment — does not apply to the findings in my chart.

### 2. Even under the standard conservative-care pathway, my records exceed what the policy asks for

The policy states:

> "Most meniscal tears WILL require documentation of non-operative treatment as follows:"

and:

> "Failure of at least 6 weeks of non-operative treatment, including at least two of the following:"

with the list including:

> "o Rest or activity modifications/limitations o Ice/heat o Protected weight bearing o Pharmacologic treatment: oral/topical NSAIDS, acetaminophen, analgesics, tramadol o Brace/orthosis o Physical therapy modalities o Supervised home exercise o Weight optimization o Corticosteroid injection"

My records establish the following:

| Plan's listed modality | What my records document |
|---|---|
| Physical therapy modalities | **Supervised physical therapy, 14 weeks**, March 30, 2026 to July 6, 2026, **24 visits completed**, focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion (physical therapy discharge note) |
| Pharmacologic treatment: oral/topical NSAIDS | **NSAIDs for 6 months** with inadequate relief |
| Corticosteroid injection | **Corticosteroid injection on April 23, 2026**, which gave only 2 weeks of partial relief |
| Rest / activity modifications | Symptoms of **12 months' duration, progressive, unrelieved by rest**; activity limited to level walking, unable to squat or kneel |

The policy asks for at least six weeks of non-operative treatment including at least two of the listed modalities. My records document 14 weeks and 24 visits of supervised physical therapy, six months of NSAIDs, and a corticosteroid injection — three of the listed modalities, over a period well beyond six weeks, with the treatment course completed and documented as unsuccessful before surgery was requested.

The policy also states:

> "The required duration of non-operative treatment will vary depending on the surgical procedure - (Example: 6 weeks for meniscectomy, 3 months for diagnostic arthroscopy, 6 months for patellofemoral procedures)."

The requested procedure is CPT 29881, and my documented course of non-operative care ran from March 30, 2026 to July 6, 2026, with medication use extending over six months.

### 3. My records contain the documentation elements the policy asks office notes to include

The policy states:

> "Office notes for arthroscopic knee surgery requests should document: o Symptom onset, duration, and severity; o Loss of function and/or limitations; o Type and duration of non-operative management modalities (where applicable)."

- **Symptom onset, duration, and severity:** 12 months of progressive knee pain, unrelieved by rest.
- **Loss of function and/or limitations:** locking and giving way; unable to squat or kneel; limited to level walking; range of motion limited by pain.
- **Type and duration of non-operative management:** as set out in the table above, with specific dates and visit counts.

### 4. The arthritis-related criteria are met by the imaging in my chart

The policy states:

> "Unless the patient has a locked knee with a displaced bucket-handle tear, weight-bearing X-rays must show no more than mild arthritis for approval of meniscus procedures. (No more than K-L 2 changes – see grading appendix*)"

My imaging of May 24, 2026 documents **articular cartilage preserved, Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1** — within the "no more than K-L 2" range the policy describes. Separately, this criterion opens with an exception for a locked knee with a displaced bucket-handle tear, which is what my MRI describes.

The policy also states:

> "For all knee arthroscopy requests, the weight-bearing status of all X-rays should be documented in the office notes. If an MRI was performed, the actual MRI report should be included in the office notes as well."

and:

> "For meniscus surgery requests, if there is evidence of associated arthritis by history, physical examination or MRI, weight-bearing X-rays are required to further establish the degree of articular cartilage loss."

My MRI was performed and the MRI report is part of the submitted records. Regarding X-rays: [weight-bearing status of any X-rays obtained — to be completed from my surgeon's office notes]. If the plan considers additional imaging documentation necessary, I ask that it tell me specifically what it needs so my surgeon's office can send it, rather than denying the surgery on conservative-care grounds that my records already address.

### 5. Request that the plan identify the criteria it applied

Several of the provisions I have quoted introduce lists, and the copy of the tip sheet excerpts available to me does not reproduce every item in every list. If the plan relied on a specific criterion I have not addressed, I ask that the appeal decision identify that criterion by name and quote it, so that I and my surgeon can respond to it directly.

---

### What I am asking for

I respectfully ask Harvard Pilgrim Health Care to overturn the denial of reference number POC-9668BA39E4-60948 and authorize knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery, CPT 29881, as requested by Marchetti, MD. The denial rests on an inadequate trial of conservative treatment; the records establish 14 weeks and 24 visits of supervised physical therapy, six months of NSAIDs, and a corticosteroid injection, as well as an MRI finding of a displaced bucket-handle tear with mechanical locking, which the policy itself identifies as a situation in which non-operative treatment is not required.

If the denial is upheld in whole or in part, I ask for a written explanation that identifies each criterion the plan applied and the specific records it reviewed, along with information about my further appeal rights, including external review.

Per the plan's notice, my appeal must be received within 180 days of the August 4, 2026 notice date — **by January 31, 2027**. I am submitting this letter to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, and I understand I may also reach Member Services by phone at **1-888-333-4742**.

I am happy to provide anything else you need, and my surgeon's office can be contacted directly for records. Thank you for taking a fresh look at this.

Sincerely,

**Emerson Hayes**
Member ID: W807153430
[Signature]
[Date]

**Enclosures:**
- Copy of denial notice dated August 4, 2026 (Reference POC-9668BA39E4-60948)
- Physical therapy discharge note (March 30, 2026 – July 6, 2026, 24 visits)
- MRI report of the knee dated May 24, 2026
- Office notes from Marchetti, MD, orthopedic surgery
- [Weight-bearing X-ray report, if obtained]
- [Any other records my surgeon's office is sending]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
```
